sections.label: Overview
sections.html:
Cloudig bookmarklets export AI conversations from their official websites as HTML files that can be read directly. In V1.0, automatic installation supports Chrome only.

Cloudig currently supports web-conversation exports from the specified official platforms only. If you want another platform supported, leave a message for the author.

sections.label: The Shortest Possible Guide
sections.html:
1. Close Chrome. To let Cloudig install, update or uninstall bookmarklets automatically, quit Chrome completely, including its background processes.
  2. Choose a bookmarklet profile and install it. Use Light for everyday exports, Full for complete attachments, and Tree for the complete branch tree.
  3. Open a specific conversation on the AI platform in Chrome.
  4. Click the bookmarklet and wait. Keep the tab being exported in the foreground and the window visible. Do not touch the page until the HTML appears in Chrome's download list.
  5. Check the HTML. Confirm that the text, turns, layout, images and files are all there.
  6. If something is missing, check two things first.
    1. Confirm the bookmarklet profile and numeric version. Light saves the text, compressed images and metadata for other files; it does not save the attachment files themselves.
    2. Refresh the original conversation, wait for everything to load, then export it again with Full or Tree if needed.
  7. Keep the original HTML. It is both directly readable and a source that future versions of Cloudig can parse again.

If the problem remains, open the System Log on the right side of Cloudig, find the errors for that file, and contact the author with the version, log, screenshots and a sanitized copy of the page.

sections.label: 1. Bookmarklet Profiles
sections.html:
Profile What it saves Images and files
Light The current branch or current linear conversation Saves compressed images; other files retain only metadata such as name and type, not the files themselves
Full The current branch or current linear conversation Saves original images and complete attachments whenever they can be obtained; does not include other branches
Tree The complete message tree Uses the same image and attachment policy as Full, and also preserves the other branches

Light is a good everyday choice and saves storage space. All three profiles can be installed at the same time; choose whichever one a particular conversation needs.

Gemini, Doubao, ChatGLM, Tencent Yuanbao, Claude Cowork and Kimi Agent mode do not support branches. Use Light or Full. Ordinary Kimi Chat does support Tree; the restriction applies only to Agent mode.

sections.label: 2. Installation and Updates
sections.html:
Automatic installation

  1. Open Cloudig and enter Archiver (档案馆).
  2. Select one profile on the left. To install several profiles, install them one after another.
  3. Choose the Chrome user and bookmark folder. The default folder is 采云 Cloudig.
  4. Quit Chrome completely, including its background processes.
  5. Install one platform, or install every selected platform at once.
  6. Reopen Chrome and confirm that the 采云 Cloudig folder appears on the bookmarks bar.
  7. Click Install All to update every bookmarklet in the currently selected profile—Light, Full or Tree—to the latest version automatically.

Figure 1. Each bookmarklet name includes the platform, profile and numeric version.

Updating the Cloudig program does not update the bookmarklets already installed in Chrome. To update them, quit Chrome completely, return to Archiver, and click Update.

Updating a bookmarklet does not change HTML files you have already downloaded. If an older HTML is complete and looks right, there is no need to download it again merely because the bookmarklet was updated.

Manual installation

  1. In Cloudig, click Copy beside the platform.
  2. Right-click the Chrome bookmarks bar and choose Add page.
  3. Enter a name, paste the complete code into the URL field, and save it.

Figure 2. Right-click the bookmarks bar and choose Add page.

Figure 3. Put the complete code in the URL field. Name it however you like.

The same method can be used to install and run the bookmarklets manually from the Microsoft Edge favorites bar.

sections.label: 3. Exporting a Conversation
sections.html:
Open a specific conversation on a platform where you are already signed in. Bookmarklets do not support settings pages, conversation-list pages or blank home pages.

  1. Wait until the text and every image, chart or attachment you want to keep are visible.
  2. Click the Cloudig bookmarklet for that platform and profile.
  3. Once you see Reading or Saving resources, do not refresh, switch conversations or click the bookmarklet again.
  4. Keep that tab selected and the Chrome window visible. Do not operate the window during the export.
  5. Wait for the bookmarklet to report completion and confirm that the HTML has appeared in the download list. You can safely leave the page after that.

Figure 4. Export in progress. Long conversations, complete resources and Tree exports take longer.

Figure 5. The HTML is in the download list, so this export is complete.

The bookmarklet may scroll the page or open panels to gather the complete content. Do not refresh or operate the page while it is doing so.

sections.label: 4. HTML and Cloudig
sections.html:
Double-click a downloaded HTML to open it in a browser. Its text, styling, formulas, static diagrams and embedded resources can be read offline. External links inside the content still require a network connection.

Keep the original HTML. It is both a directly readable archive and a source that a future Cloudig parser can process again.

After importing the HTML into Cloudig, you also gain:

  • unified offline reading and centralized management across platforms;
  • filtering by folder, platform and model;
  • title, display-name and identity settings;
  • ContentTime settings;
  • more recording and reading features as Cloudig continues to evolve.

Explore the platform examples →

sections.label: 5. When Content Is Missing
sections.html:
Start with two checks:

  1. Check the bookmarklet profile and numeric version. Light does not contain non-image attachment files and uses compressed images; Full does not contain other branches.
  2. Refresh the original conversation, wait for it to finish loading, confirm the platform, profile and version, then export again. Network fluctuations, server conditions, lazy loading and temporary resource URLs can make a second export succeed.

If that does not solve the problem, open the System Log on the right side of Archiver or Reader:

  1. Find the log for the affected file.
  2. Copy the relevant error text.
  3. Contact the author with the material that demonstrates the problem.

The presence of System Log entries does not by itself mean that the archive is damaged, or even that anything is missing. What matters is a human check:

  • Does the HTML open?
  • Are all conversation turns present and in the right order?
  • Do code, formulas, tables, charts and layout look right?
  • Do images and files match the selected bookmarklet profile?

Figure 6. You can copy one entry or every error for the file and trace each one to its source. Deleting a log does not affect the HTML or the archive.

sections.label: 6. Four Different Kinds of Update
sections.html:
Action What it changes When you need it
Update Cloudig Reader, Parser, Archiver and desktop features When you want new Cloudig features
Update Chrome bookmarklets How future content is obtained from the website When a new version fixes a platform problem you care about
Download the HTML again Returns to the website to obtain content or files again When the old HTML is genuinely missing something and the newer bookmarklet fixes it
Parse again in Cloudig Uses the newer Parser to generate new JSON from the existing HTML When the HTML already contains the content but the older Parser did not parse it correctly

If an older HTML is complete and looks right, a bookmarklet update alone is not a reason to download it again.

sections.label: 7. Contacting the Author
sections.html:
Please include as much of the following as possible:

  • the platform and entry point, such as Chat, Cowork or Agent;
  • the full bookmarklet name and numeric version;
  • which turn, image or file is affected, and what went wrong;
  • a screenshot of the affected area;
  • the System Log text;
  • an HTML with anything you do not want to disclose removed, or an official Share Link.
